chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) married Duba'ah bint al-Zubayr, daughter of al-Zubayr ibn Abd al-Muttalib, to Miqdad ibn al-Aswad. So the Banu Hashim spoke about that, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I only intended that the marriages be humble/lowly.'

key_terms.بَنُو هَاشِمٍ: Banu Hashim, the clan of the Prophet
key_terms.ضُبَاعَةَ: Duba'ah, a daughter of al-Zubayr ibn Abd al-Muttalib
key_terms.مِقْدَادِ بْنِ الْأَسْوَدِ: Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, a companion of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet Muhammad marry Dubaah bint al-Zubayr to Miqdad ibn al-Aswad?
ai.summary: This hadith, found in the chapter on *Kafa'ah* (spousal compatibility), illustrates the Prophet's deliberate choice to marry his cousin to Miqdad, a former slave of humble origins, to challenge the pre-Islamic Arab obsession with lineage. By stating his intent was for marriages to be characterized by humility (*tadhi' al-manakih*), he established a theological precedent that spiritual merit and piety outweigh social stratification, a key principle in Shia jurisprudence regarding marital eligibility.
